subject: scripts/schedule.py (actl schedule plan|run): DAG from tickets' depends_on + board/batches.json edited by main; dispatches auto-fix.sh up to schedule.max_workers, lands each all-green batch with land.sh t<a> t<b> …, wakes main only at terminal states; ticket.py lint rejects depends_on cycles
objective: User (2026-10-25): 「票的 DAG 應該可以跟 land.sh 1 2 3 連動…land.sh t162 t164 t165 應該是系統自動知道的,不是 llm 去控制的…LLM 應該是依我的要求去改 dag 的 batch 檔案,後面的 land 該怎麼跑應該是自動的」「開題者要在開題時把自己的票插入 dag」. D-073 ② (batch landing), D-067 (no polling; wake main only at terminal states), D-049 ④ (DAG). Rewritten after the subtraction audit (D-054): no queue platform, no PlanningBatch manifest, no slot API - one script over facts that already exist (ticket files, git, auto-fix.sh, land.sh, inbox.py). (1) scripts/schedule.py with 'plan' (read-only) and 'run'; bin/actl TABLE row 'schedule' and the case that execs it. (2) DAG: nodes = tickets in tickets_dir, edges = depends_on. A dependency is satisfied iff the dependency ticket is Done AND its landed_sha is an ancestor of main (git merge-base --is-ancestor) - 'Done' alone or a non-empty sha alone is not enough. Condition 'landed' (and legacy '落地…' / '已落地…' on Done tickets) is the only understood condition; any other string, a missing ticket, or a Cancelled/Blocked dependency -> the dependant is 'waiting(<reason>)', never dispatched, reason printed. A cycle or self-dependency among tickets that are not Done/Cancelled -> rc 2 naming the cycle; nothing starts. (3) Batch file board/batches.json, edited by main on the user's request: {"schema": 1, "batches": [{"id": "b1", "tickets": ["162", "164", "165"]}, {"id": "b2", "tickets": ["163", "166"]}, {"id": "b3", "tickets": ["167"]}]} - list order is landing order. Validation (rc 2, naming ticket / dependency / batch): unknown id, an id listed twice, invalid JSON, schema != 1, a dependency inside the same batch (gates are measured against main, not against a batch-mate), a dependency in a later batch or in no batch and not landed. Tickets not listed are untouched by run and printed under 'unscheduled'. File absent -> default plan: batch = every Ready ticket whose dependencies are all landed; after it lands, recompute (next frontier) until nothing is Ready or the frontier is empty while tickets wait (then stop and list why). (4) run, per batch: tickets already green (InReview, gate pass; complex also review.verdict pass per ticket.py review_problems) count as green without dispatch; Ready tickets get 'sh $AC_HOME/scripts/auto-fix.sh <n>' spawned (cwd AC_ROOT) with at most schedule.max_workers (board/config.json, default 2; one auto-fix = one worker + at most one verifier, 4 CPUs) running at once; the script blocks on its children (subprocess wait) - nobody polls status files. auto-fix rc 0 -> green. Any other rc -> that ticket is red-terminal for this run (auto-fix already wrote its own decision page): running children finish, no new dispatch in this batch, then stop (6). A ticket that is Running / InReview-without-gate at start -> rc 2 before anything starts ('another driver has #n'); complex InReview without a review verdict -> 'waiting(review)', counted not green, and if nothing else can move the run stops with a decision page naming review.sh. (5) All tickets of the batch green -> foreground 'sh $AC_HOME/scripts/land.sh <branch…>' (branch = ticket's branch field, else t<n>; batch-file order). land rc 0 -> land closed the tickets -> recompute, next batch. land rc != 0 -> stop (land did its batch_fix and pages; the scheduler never re-runs land). (6) Terminal states, exactly one inbox page per run: every listed batch landed -> kind done, attached to the last landed ticket, listing batches and landed shas; any stop -> kind decision attached to the ticket that stopped it: what happened, what main does next (handle that ticket's page / edit board/batches.json / run review.sh), and 'actl schedule run' to resume. Nothing to dispatch or land at start -> rc 3, reasons on stdout, no page (DISPATCH-TEMPLATE §5.5: 'nothing to do' must not look like 'done'). Events: schedule.start (kv run_id, batches, max_workers), schedule.dispatch per ticket, schedule.land per batch (kv branches), schedule.stop (kv reason). Log: reports/schedule/<run_id>/schedule.log + plan.json. (7) Resumable: nothing is persisted but logs; run recomputes from ticket files and git at start and after every land. Lock .schedule.lock (mkdir, like land's) -> second run rc 2 naming the holder. The scheduler never signals a child (no kill of any spelling): auto-fix and land own their timeouts. (8) 'ticket.py lint <n>' gains: depends_on cycle / self-dependency across tickets_dir -> rc 1 line 'depends_on cycle: a -> b -> a'; a condition other than 'landed' on the linted ticket -> rc 1 naming it; lint stays read-only. This is how an opener 'inserts a ticket into the DAG': write depends_on, run lint. Not here: a board view of the plan (plan's stdout is the view), PlanningBatch manifests (#118), session registry / slot API (#117), scope-overlap serialisation (D-054 Q2 removed write scopes; land.sh's merge conflict stop and batch_fix are the overlap handling), Controller (#120).
acceptance: A1 plan / DAG (tests/test_schedule.py, harness sandbox, tickets written by the test; 'actl schedule plan', no batches.json): A Ready no deps; B Ready depends A landed; C Ready depends #999 (missing); D Ready depends E, E Ready depends D; F Done landed_sha = a commit on the sandbox main; G Ready depends F; H Ready depends F with condition '閘門綠'; J Ready depends K, K Done with landed_sha = a sha not in the sandbox repo -> rc 2 and stdout names the cycle 'D -> E -> D' (both ids), nothing else printed as a batch; after the test removes D and E: rc 0, stdout has 'batch 1: A G' (ids ascending), waiting lines: B 'waiting dep #A not landed', C 'waiting missing #999', H "waiting unknown condition '閘門綠'", J 'waiting dep #K landed_sha not on main'. No process spawned (fake auto-fix call log absent), no inbox page, every ticket file byte-identical, no event emitted by plan.

A2 batches.json validation (same file): b1 [A, B] -> rc 2 naming B, A and 'same batch'; b1 [B], b2 [A] -> rc 2 naming B, A, 'later batch'; b1 [A] with B unlisted -> rc 0, stdout 'b1: A' then 'unscheduled: B'; id '777' -> rc 2 naming 777; A listed in b1 and b2 -> rc 2 'twice'; invalid JSON -> rc 2 naming board/batches.json; schema 2 -> rc 2 naming 'schema'. In every rc-2 arm nothing is spawned and no page is written.

A3 dispatch and concurrency (same file; fake auto-fix.sh in the sandbox ac-home appends '<n> start <epoch>' and '<n> end <epoch>' to a call log, sleeps 2 s, sets the ticket InReview with a gate pass, exits 0): b1 [A, G, X] all Ready, schedule.max_workers 2 -> call log has three start/end pairs and the maximum number of overlapping intervals is exactly 2; max_workers 1 -> no overlap and the three starts are in batch order; A already InReview with gate pass (complex: plus review.verdict pass) -> no call for A, A is in the land argv; a complex A InReview without review -> no call for A, A not landed, the run stops with one decision page whose text contains 'review.sh' and '#A'; X Running at start -> rc 2 before any call (empty call log) naming X and 'another driver'.

A4 land chaining (same file; fake land.sh records argv, sets each named ticket Done with landed_sha = the sandbox main HEAD it advances by one commit, exits 0): b1 [A, G, X], b2 [B] (B depends A) -> exactly one land call for b1 with argv 'tA tG tX' in batch order (ticket branch field used when set: X with branch 'tX-renamed' -> that name), B's dispatch line comes after the b1 land line in the call log, a second land call 'tB', then run rc 0, exactly one inbox page (kind done, ticket B) listing b1 and b2 with both landed shas, events in order: schedule.start, schedule.dispatch ×4, schedule.land ×2, schedule.stop reason=done. Mutation (not measured by opener): m1 land called when only 2 of 3 are green -> this assertion red (argv count).

A5 stops (same file): max_workers 1, fake auto-fix exits 1 for G -> X never dispatched, land never called, run rc 1, exactly one decision page naming G and 'actl schedule run' and 'board/batches.json', A's state unchanged (InReview), schedule.stop reason=red; fake land exits 1 -> run rc 1, land called exactly once, no b2 dispatch, one decision page naming b1 and 'land'. No batches.json, all Ready tickets waiting on an un-landed Done-without-sha dependency -> rc 3, stdout lists each 'waiting' reason, no page, no dispatch. Every ticket Done -> rc 3, stdout 'nothing to dispatch or land', no page.

A6 lock and resume (same file): with .schedule.lock present (holder file 'pid=1 …') -> run rc 2 naming the holder, nothing spawned; a run that stopped at A5's red, re-run after the test sets G InReview+gate pass -> dispatches nothing for A/G, dispatches X, lands b1 (argv 'tA tG tX') - i.e. recompute from facts, no state file needed (the test deletes reports/schedule/ first).

A7 lint (tests/test_ticket.py): D <-> E cycle -> 'ticket.py lint D' rc 1 with a line containing 'depends_on cycle' and both ids; self-dependency -> rc 1; condition '閘門綠' -> rc 1 naming the condition and 'landed'; a ticket whose dependency is Done with a legacy '落地(…)' condition -> rc 0 (legacy on Done is read as landed); lint on A (no deps) still prints 'lint #A ok'; lint leaves every ticket file byte-identical and emits no event. 'ticket.py create --depends-on 7:閘門綠' is still accepted (lint is the check, D-031).

outline: Rewritten 2026-10-25 by the opener from the user's words (DAG ↔ land.sh linkage is the system's, the LLM edits the batch file; openers insert tickets into the DAG = depends_on). Facts at base 1b6ac4e: no script reads depends_on today (grep: only board.py renders it); land.sh maps branch t<n>[-…] -> ticket (376-390), refuses 0 commits / stale base_sha / hard_block / complex without review (ticket.py review_problems, objection_problems), takes .land.lock by mkdir (90-110), runs batch_fix itself and writes its own decision pages; auto-fix.sh <n> starts round 1 for a Ready ticket, rc table in its header (0 green incl. review pass; 1/3/4/5/6/7/8/9/10 stops) and writes decision pages for its stops; inbox.py post kinds are decision / done only (INBOX_KINDS); ticket.py lint 1664-1681 only checks tags (no cycle check) - add one; depends_on conditions in the ticket store: 50 'landed' (all open tickets), legacy '落地…' / '已落地…' / '' / 'stacked:…' only on Done/Cancelled tickets; states IntegrationQueued / Integrating exist in STATES but no script sets them (not used here either - land owns state). Judgement on the former prerequisites: #101 Done (its write-scope hints were later deleted by D-054 Q2; dependency dropped as satisfied-and-irrelevant); #117 (session registry v2, slot API) dropped from depends_on - the only thing #119 needed from it was a process slot, and a counter over the scheduler's own children is that; recommend keeping #117 Draft for the main to decide with its cluster (#120/#123/#124/#125), not a #119 matter; #118 (PlanningBatch manifest) recommend Cancel: superseded by this ticket's rule 'opener writes depends_on + lint checks cycles' and by board/batches.json for ordering - the user's words put the DAG in the tickets, not in a manifest. #93 stays frozen on #119 landing (D-050 ④) - unchanged. Depends on #162 (auto-fix/land/gate on testiface; scheduler calls them). complex. needs_verifier true, interface_fixed true. Not measured: the mutations; real 'run' in A (worker must not run it).
test_plan: Layers: unit (tests/test_schedule.py, harness Sandbox with the per-test ac-home copy whose auto-fix.sh / land.sh / review.sh are replaced by recording fakes, as test_land does with gate_stub; oracles are the fakes' call logs, the ticket files the fakes write and hand-written expected strings - never schedule.py's own output parsed back), unit (tests/test_ticket.py for lint), static/dogfood A8. Worker, foreground: timeout 590 python3 -m unittest tests.test_schedule; then tests.test_ticket; then tests.test_actl (TABLE row) and the base command once. Verifier (needs_verifier true, interface_fixed true: subcommands, batches.json schema 1, rc table 0/1/2/3, event names, page kinds and config key are pinned here) writes tests/test_schedule_cases.py in parallel: a Done dependency whose landed_sha is NOT an ancestor of main is not satisfied (the 'Done alone is not enough' rule, old A3); a batch whose land fails must not let a later batch's dependant dispatch; a ticket with legacy '落地(…)' condition on a Done dependency is dispatched; max_workers absent -> 2 (overlap == 2 with 3 tickets); two runs started together -> exactly one proceeds (lock). Mutations (not measured by opener): m1 as A4; m2 'Done' accepted without ancestry -> A1 J arm red; m3 max_workers ignored -> A3 overlap red; m4 cycle check removed -> A1 and A7 red; m5 lock ignored -> A6 red; m6 page written on rc 3 -> A5 last arm red. Timing margins: fakes sleep 2 s, overlap computed from epoch pairs. Container is uid 0; hard_block.patterns forbids os.kill / killpg / pkill / 'kill -' in added tests/** lines and the scheduler itself never signals children (A8 grep).
feature: agent-control: DAG scheduling and batch landing

interface_contracts.cli: actl schedule plan | run; plan is read-only (no spawn, no page, no event); run rc 0 all batches landed / 1 stopped (page written) / 2 refused before start (cycle, batch file, lock, Running ticket) / 3 nothing to do (no page).
interface_contracts.batch_file: board/batches.json {schema:1, batches:[{id, tickets:[ticket ids as strings]}]}; list order = landing order; absent = frontier default.
interface_contracts.config: board/config.json schedule.max_workers int >= 1, default 2 (one auto-fix.sh child = one slot).
interface_contracts.satisfied_dependency: dependency ticket state Done AND landed_sha is an ancestor of main_branch; condition 'landed' (legacy '落地…'/'已落地…' read as landed on Done tickets); anything else = waiting, printed.
interface_contracts.children: sh $AC_HOME/scripts/auto-fix.sh <n> and sh $AC_HOME/scripts/land.sh <branches>, cwd AC_ROOT, waited on; never signalled.
interface_contracts.events_pages: schedule.start / schedule.dispatch / schedule.land / schedule.stop; one inbox page per run (done or decision), none on rc 2/3.
